outcome: pre-eclampsia or eclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension
cohort: The study included 13,868 pregnancies after abdominal myomectomy and 338 pregnancies after laparoscopic myomectomy from hospital discharges between 2004 and 2014.
finding: Pregnant women with prior laparoscopic myomectomy experienced decreased rates of pregnancy complications but higher risks of severe intrapartum and postpartum complications including uterine rupture, hemorrhage, and death, compared to those with prior abdominal myomectomy, who had more underlying risk factors for hypertension and gestational diabetes.
mod_finding: Laparoscopic myomectomy was associated with decreased rates of cesarean delivery and increased rates of spontaneous and operative vaginal delivery compared to abdominal myomectomy.
